newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends weaker as NY indifferent to data.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends weaker as NY indifferent to data.

text.p: Trade selling kept robusta futures pinned at the lows in solid volume on Wednesday after the failure of the arabica market to react to bullish green stocks data, traders said.

London futures slid across the board in later trade with the spot November contract touching nearby support at $1,515 a tonne. But earlier, robustas firmed in reaction to the bullish stocks draw figures released late on Tuesday.
"We had a blip in late morning but basically traders were waiting for New York's reaction (to the data)," said one trader.
"When New York didn't do much after an initial rise, sellers stepped in and there were no buyers around," he said.

Supplies of green coffee held in U.S. warehouses fell by 205,000 60-kilo bags to 1,611,000 bags in September, the lowest since the Green Coffee Association (GCA) of New York began tracking inventories in 1988.
London traders said while they viewed the GCA stocks fall as higher than expected, their New York counterparts said it was within expectations.
The robusta market finished weaker across the board, with all positions either at or just hovering above intraday lows.
November closed $12 weaker at $1,516 and January down $26 at $1,433. Overall volume reached 4,524 lots.
Traders cited shortcovering of positions and industry fixing on the key November/January spread, which saw an erratic session trading from $70 to $65 in the morning and then back out to $80.
Another trader said fund players would probably focus on the spread when it came to bailing out of November before expiry.
"I think you're likely to see the movement on the switches rather than the outright when the funds decide to roll their positions," he said.
